name: Money Laundering Networks
title: Money Laundering Networks
answer: Money laundering networks are the people, companies, accounts, and intermediaries that move illicit funds to hide their origin and ownership. In fraud detection and forensics, the scope covers finding these networks, mapping their structure, tracing the flow of value, and producing evidence that stands up to review. The work sits between financial crime compliance, forensic accounting, and data analysis, and it often involves shell companies, layered transfers, trade transactions, and crypto assets. AI enters as a pattern-finding aid across large volumes of transactions, corporate records, and communications, not as a replacement for investigator judgment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Money laundering networks are the people, companies, accounts, and intermediaries that move illicit funds to hide their origin and ownership. In fraud detection and forensics, the scope covers finding these networks, mapping their structure, tracing the flow of value, and producing evidence that stands up to review. The work sits between financial crime compliance, forensic accounting, and data analysis, and it often involves shell companies, layered transfers, trade transactions, and crypto assets. AI enters as a pattern-finding aid across large volumes of transactions, corporate records, and communications, not as a replacement for investigator judgment.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on transaction data from core banking and payment systems, customer due diligence records, sanctions and politically exposed person lists, and case management platforms. Graph databases and entity resolution services are common because the central question is who is connected to whom and through which accounts or companies. Streaming pipelines and batch data lakes feed models that score alerts, while investigators work in review queues and document management systems. Compute may be cloud or on premises, and access controls, encryption, and audit logging are part of the basic plumbing.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts start with typologies such as structuring, smurfing, rapid pass-through accounts, and trade-based laundering, then translate those patterns into features and rules. Graph algorithms detect communities, central nodes, and unusual paths, while anomaly detection and sequence models flag transactions that deviate from expected behavior. Entity resolution links names, addresses, and corporate records so that one network is not split across many false identities. Natural language processing can extract entities and relationships from suspicious activity reports, invoices, and emails, but human investigators validate findings and document the reasoning. The output is usually a prioritized case file, a network diagram, and a narrative that explains why the activity is suspicious.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on lawful basis, proportionality, privacy, and the confidentiality of suspicious activity reporting. False positives can harm innocent customers, so teams track alert quality, bias, and the impact of automated decisions, and they keep model documentation and audit trails. Provenance matters for training data, entity resolution, and any evidence that may be used in a legal or regulatory process, including chain of custody and version history. The site's 215 compliance and regulation pages reflect how many rules, guidance notes, and supervisory expectations surround this work. Cross-border data sharing and vendor due diligence add further constraints, and practices vary by jurisdiction.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel includes real-time monitoring, graph neural networks, and privacy-enhancing techniques such as federated learning and secure computation. Generative AI is being tested for investigator summaries, alert triage, and document review, with human review kept in the loop for high-impact decisions. Crypto tracing, decentralized finance, and new payment rails are expanding the surface that networks can use, so forensic teams are adding on-chain analytics to their toolkits. The site tracks 147 active AI lawsuits, and disputes over automated decisions may shape how evidence from these systems is treated. Expect more focus on explainability, data provenance, and cross-institution collaboration, though adoption will remain uneven across jurisdictions.
